svg-wave-divider-generator.formula:
Smooth wave:
y = mid + amplitude × sin(2π × x / wavelength + phase)

Double wave:
y = mid + amplitude × (sin(2πx/λ) + 0.5 × sin(4πx/λ)) / 1.5

Zigzag (triangle):
t = (x / λ) mod 1
y = mid + amplitude × (4t − 1) for t < 0.5, else (3 − 4t)

Each layer adds a phase shift of 2π / layers.

keyFacts: A wave divider is an SVG shape placed between page sections so one section flows into the next with a curved edge instead of a hard line.
This generator samples the wave function every 12 pixels across a 1440-pixel-wide canvas, producing 121 path points — smooth on screen, small in file size.
The exported SVG uses preserveAspectRatio="none", so it stretches to any screen width without gaps or distortion.
Multiple layers are the same wave with a phase shift; lower layers render slightly more transparent for a sense of depth.
Flip vertically turns a bottom divider into a top divider — handy when a coloured section sits above plain content.

svg-wave-divider-generator.workedExample:
Settings: width 1440, height 320, amplitude 80, wavelength 720, smooth sine.
1. Midline = 320 / 2 = 160.
2. x = 0: sin(0) = 0 → y = 160.
3. x = 180: sin(π/2) = 1 → y = 160 + 80 = 240.
4. x = 360: sin(π) = 0 → y = 160.
5. x = 540: sin(3π/2) = −1 → y = 160 − 80 = 80.
6. x = 720: sin(2π) = 0 → y = 160.
Path: M0,320 L0,160 L180,240 L360,160 L540,80 L720,160 … L1440,160 L1440,320 Z.
The real tool samples every 12 px (121 points); the steps above are widened to 180 px so the math is easy to check by hand.
